clue.text: University let contractor into fabrications with joint commission

indicators.note: into says the university letter and the renter go inside the word for lies

parts.note: fabrications are lies
a tenant is the party who contracts to take a let property
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A university lets a building firm into a web of lies while sharing a commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let contractor' reads like a builder being allowed in; it is the person who signs a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant's rank is held by a military commission, so the office itself is a commission.

clue.text: Area, miles out, in polluted yard, say

indicators.note: in places the jumbled area-and-miles letters inside the word for polluted

parts.note: polluted means impure

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of area and miles are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone describes an area, miles across, within a contaminated yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes ERIALMEAS and 'in' sets it inside the word for polluted. 'say' marks the yard as only one example of the system.
explanation.definitionFit: The yard is one unit of the old British system of weights and lengths, so it is an example.

clue.text: Topless escort covers booby in clingy garment

indicators.note: covers means the shortened escort wraps around the fool
Topless means the first letter of the escort word is removed

parts.note: a guard escorts and protects someone
a booby is a fool, a nit

explanation.surface: A risqué image of a topless escort covering a breast inside a tight outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' and 'booby' are there for the saucy surface; 'covers' wraps the shortened escort round the fool. NIT is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A unitard is a one-piece skin-tight leotard covering the body and legs.

clue.text: Are you in Paris informally? First sign where bores may be found

parts.note: the familiar French for are you is es-tu
Aries is the first sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A question in casual French, then an astrology note about where tiresome people lurk.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore here is a tidal wave surging up a river mouth, like the Severn bore in England, not a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal bores form where the incoming sea funnels into wide river mouths.

clue.text: Tools peripherally supporting computer business?

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means this part sits below the computer company

parts.note: Apple is a well-known computer company

indicators.note: peripherally picks only the outside letters of the word tools

explanation.surface: A question about gadgets that back up a computer firm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supporting' puts TS (from 'peripherally') under APPLE. The whole clue doubles as a description of little programs.
explanation.definitionFit: Small programs that run inside another application work as tools on a computer, apt for a computer business.

clue.text: This mark is wavy line in moving sea

indicators.note: in puts the single letter for line inside the word for the moving sea

parts.note: the tide is the sea moving in and out

explanation.surface: Somebody points to a squiggle drawn in a rolling sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the squiggly accent placed over letters such as the Spanish n.

clue.text: Bed workers welcoming periodical tributes

indicators.note: welcoming means the garden tools take the magazine inside them

parts.note: hoes are tools used to work flower beds
a mag is a periodical, a magazine

explanation.surface: Staff in a bedroom greeting a magazine as it arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests sleep; it is a flower bed, worked with hoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Homages are acts of respect or honour paid to someone, tributes.

clue.text: Pressure faction to embrace talents wasted where convictions may lead one

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: to embrace says the faction word wraps around the scrambled talents

parts.note: an element is a faction or group within a larger body

indicators.note: wasted signals the letters of talents are squandered into a new order

explanation.surface: A pressure group taking in squandered gifts, ending where guilty verdicts send people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' makes NALSETT, which 'to embrace' places inside the faction word. 'convictions' looks like beliefs but means guilty verdicts in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal settlement is a colony where convicted criminals were transported, like those in Australia.

clue.text: Flip out unexpectedly, forgetting old exaltation

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters of flip out are rearranged surprisingly

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper out of nowhere, setting aside an old sense of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle FLIP OUT ('unexpectedly'), 'forgetting' the O for old, and the remaining six letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplift is a raising of the spirits, an elevation of mood.

clue.text: Golden horse, one of many toppling when China ousts leader?

indicators.note: ousts leader means the first letter is pushed out and replaced

parts.note: a domino is one of a long row knocked over in a chain
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a horse falls like a domino when China removes its ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A palomino has a golden coat with a pale mane and tail.

clue.text: Some ogre at a penitentiary is a relative of ours

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A monster in prison turns out to be one of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas and chimpanzees are humanity's nearest primate cousins.

clue.text: Electronic news-gathering spun virus and flood

parts.note: ENG is the broadcasting abbreviation for electronic news-gathering

indicators.note: spun means the word for virus is turned round

parts.note: flu is caused by a virus

explanation.surface: TV news coverage puts a spin on a virus outbreak and floods.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to swamp or overwhelm, as rising water does.

clue.text: Pacific nationalist initially going along with Hawaii

indicators.note: initially picks only the opening letter of going

parts.note: along with means and
HI is the US postal abbreviation for Hawaii

explanation.surface: An island nationalist from the Pacific heading off with Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' looks like the ocean beside Hawaii; here it means peaceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Gandhi led India's independence movement by nonviolent resistance, a peaceful patriot.

clue.text: Visionary has master established in academic half-year

indicators.note: has means the visionary word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a seer is a visionary, a prophet
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A prophet has a master's degree set up in a college term.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is one of two terms dividing a college year.

clue.text: TV attorney nailing wrong side with episodes still to air?

indicators.note: nailing means the lawyer pins the jumbled letters inside himself

parts.note: Perry Mason is the famous lawyer of the US TV series

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of side are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A television lawyer nails the guilty side while more episodes remain unbroadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes IDSE, which 'nailing' puts inside the lawyer, a pun on an attorney nailing a culprit.
explanation.definitionFit: A season part-way through has later episodes yet to be broadcast.

clue.text: US-manned buggy for explorer

indicators.note: buggy, meaning faulty, signals the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying an American crew for a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a vehicle for the explorer, but it means faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen was the Norwegian explorer first to reach the South Pole.

clue.text: I hate that time in drama preceding initial item in series!

indicators.note: in places the cry of disgust and the time letter inside the drama word

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer moans about the bit before the opening act of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming before the first in a sequence means being numbered zero.

clue.text: Relish minutes in the morning with nobleman shortly rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the whole sequence is read from bottom to top

parts.note: AM means in the morning

indicators.note: shortly cuts the last letter from the nobleman

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone takes a condiment early in the day with an aristocrat getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims COUNT to COUN; M + AM + COUN read upward ('rising') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuoc mam is a Vietnamese fish sauce used as a condiment.

clue.text: Weak old music-maker led by investigator

indicators.note: led by means the instrument comes after the investigator

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
the lute is an old stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A feeble antique instrument guided by a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Watered down or thinned, a diluted drink is weaker.

clue.text: Expunge duke from large file on person with less fidelity

indicators.note: Expunge means the letter for duke is struck out of the file

parts.note: a dossier is a file of information on someone

explanation.surface: Wiping a duke from a big file on someone less faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fidelity' suggests faithfulness, but it is audio or data quality: lossy compression throws data away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lossy data compression discards detail, so a lossier copy reproduces its source less accurately.

clue.text: Irish police besieging upper-class Indonesian airline

indicators.note: besieging means the police surround the class letter

parts.note: the Garda is the police force of Ireland
U denotes upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Irish officers surrounding a posh airline from Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Garuda Indonesia is the country's national flag carrier.

clue.text: Evidence of computerised intelligence entrapping Liberal

indicators.note: entrapping means the intelligence abbreviation closes around the party word

parts.note: AI is artificial intelligence

explanation.surface: Proof that a computer system has snared a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof of being elsewhere when a crime occurred.

clue.text: Exceed votes per casting constituents

indicators.note: casting, as in casting about or recasting, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Going beyond the limit on votes each constituent can cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting constituents' hints at voters; 'casting' shuffles the letters that make up VOTES PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to go beyond a limit or boundary.

clue.text: English with elevated drone about represents flowery language

parts.note: up means raised, elevated

indicators.note: about means the drone word goes around the other word

parts.note: a hum is a low drone
is can mean represents, as in this symbol is a heart

explanation.surface: An English speaker with a raised drone shows off ornate prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphuism is an affected, ornate prose style named after Lyly's Euphues.

clue.text: Movement of hips, perhaps rotating weight in jeans

indicators.note: rotating means the whole assembled word is turned round
in puts the weight letter inside the jeans brand

parts.note: Levi's is a brand of jeans

explanation.surface: Hips swinging, with weight shifting in tight jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotating' reverses LEVIS with W inside, giving the answer; Levi's is the denim brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A swivel is a turning motion, such as one of the hips.

clue.text: Runners-up in race results?

parts.note: reads as competitors placed behind the winner, but race means a people of shared descent and runners-up a smaller group

explanation.surface: A question about the placings at the end of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A group smaller in number than the majority population, of distinct descent, is a demographic subgroup.
